# Not handing an executor work it has already been handed

Under an idempotent cascade mode, a re-run whose resolved inputs equal a
predecessor's is dropped before the executor. Inputs that differ still dispatch.

## The template

A sender cascades to itself four times. The receiver subscribes to every
attribute change the sender emits, so it is cascaded four times.

```yaml
name: idempotent-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: a
    kind: loop_counter
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:   {type: integer, default: 4}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: b
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    cascade_mode: idempotent-queue
    subscribes:
      - node: a
        type: attribute/*
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          snapshot:
            type: integer
            source: "{{nodes.a.attribute.max}}"
```

`{{nodes.a.attribute.max}}` never changes, so all four rounds resolve to a
byte-identical bag.

## What the product does

Count the receiver's `work_started` events — the number of times its executor
was actually reached:

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
```

Under `cascade_mode: sequenced` — the control — all four rounds reach the
executor, each carrying `{"snapshot": 4}`.

Under `cascade_mode: idempotent-queue`, the same four rounds produce exactly one
dispatch. The three re-runs whose inputs equalled a predecessor never reached
the executor.

Under `cascade_mode: idempotent-settled`, the same: one dispatch out of four.

## The drop follows from input equality

Change the receiver to read a value that differs each round:

```yaml
          snapshot:
            type: integer
            source: "{{nodes.a.attribute.count}}"
```

Both idempotent modes now dispatch all four rounds, carrying four distinct bags.
The drop is not cascade rounds being coalesced; it is inputs being equal.

## Choosing between the two modes

`idempotent-queue` compares against the queued predecessor.
`idempotent-settled` also compares against the most recent settled run. Both
behave the same way on identical and on differing inputs, so pick between them
on how far back the comparison should reach.
